WP1.notes:
Improvements inside my files:
(1) coverageMap flattens each identity key with String.prototype.normalize(), falling back to the original text in the never-seen case where normalize would change it. In V8 a concatenated key is a tree of its parts, and the map keeps that tree alive. Measured on Node 24 for 2,000,000 PTP identities: 345 MiB without flattening, 178 MiB with it. The design estimated 300 MiB.
(2) ContentSummaryBuilder re-merges a content's windows once it holds 4,096 more than at its last merge. This keeps its memory to a few ranges per content even over millions of drafts records, which serves the CLI's file-by-file reading (m8).
(3) coverageRegression reads nextRecords in a single pass, and only when some open source-dated loss needs its closing record checked.
(4) subtractRanges uses one moving pointer over the sorted subtrahend, so it runs in O(n+m) after sorting.
(5) A second m3 test makes content/outgoing a regular file. That gives ENOTDIR, which must also throw, so the 'only ENOENT is swallowed' rule is tested even as root, where the mode-000 test skips.
(6) The previousReleaseNumber readdir carries the /*turbopackIgnore: true*/ comment, as releaseDirOf and impact's releaseDirectory do.
(7) contentOf throws a TypeError naming the key, in canonical JSON, when an mppr_rate key has neither hcpcs nor component.

- renderCoverageFile writes keys in schema order and sorts key names (canonical order) inside each loss key.
